adoption.rationale: The exact Base64URL encoder feeds WebAuthn credential JSON fields such as rawId, authenticatorData, clientDataJSON, signatures, and attestationObject. The WebAuthn JSON conversion path names this representation, and RFC 4648 section 5 defines its URL-safe alphabet and optional omitted padding. The contract is limited to the encoder output; it does not claim authentication, decoder rejection of malformed input, or server-side credential validity.

contract.input_source: ArrayBuffer values from PublicKeyCredential.rawId and AuthenticatorResponse fields returned by the browser API.

adoption.rationale: binToUrlBase64 creates each DPoP JWS compact component from the JSON header/claims bytes and Web Crypto signature bytes. The transformation removes padding and maps the two standard Base64 symbols to the URL-safe alphabet before dot-joining the three components. RFC 7515 requires these protected-header, payload, and signature components to use unpadded Base64URL. The contract covers this output mapping only; it does not claim DPoP claim validity, key custody, or server acceptance.

contract.declared_domain: The reachable DPoP components are passed through the exact source replacement chain. The Z3 theorem is per input codepoint with no length bound; exact Node replay covers all one- and two-byte inputs, representative JSON text, and seeded byte buffers.

contract.input_source: Binary JSON header/claims and signature bytes generated by the pinned DPoP implementation and Web Crypto signing API.
